Neither result was sufficient to confirm what kind of organization currently occupies this Maricopa County address, what it does, or whether it operates any data center infrastructure at all. Given the healthcare tag on the same record, the more plausible reading is a small office for a health technology or clinical services business running its own internal systems, not a commercial or enterprise data center. This entry records that uncertainty honestly rather than describing capacity, tenants or infrastructure that could not be verified.

reading.body:
Myndshift Technologies in Maricopa County, Arizona, is an unconfirmed data center with zero published megawatts, and the available evidence points to a small healthcare technology office rather than commercial compute infrastructure.

The OpenStreetMap record for this address carries both a data center tag and a healthcare specialty tag for neurology, an inconsistency that suggests a health technology or clinical office rather than a facility built to house server racks and cooling for outside customers. The myndshift.com domain is listed for sale, while myndshift.io blocks automated access, and reverse geocoding of the coordinates returns no business name. None of this confirms any data center infrastructure.

The published megawatt figure is zero, but that reflects absence of disclosure rather than measured load. Because no operator has published power, cooling capacity, or floor space, no inference about rack count, accelerator hosting, or grid load is possible. Arizona has 56 mapped data center locations, but only 4 publish megawatt figures, totaling 512 MW. This facility cannot be ranked by power capacity and should not be included in any model of the state's AI compute footprint until an operator publishes specifications or independent confirmation of commercial operations is obtained.
